winner.title: Moambe Chicken (Poulet à la Moambé)

evidence.authenticity: Peanut-butter version (adapted from Margarita's International Recipes) cooked in red palm oil, so it is the Mwambe Nsusu variant rather than the palm-nut-cream original. The author is a Minnesota-born home cook, not Congolese. His post separates DR Congo from Republic of Congo, notes French and Belgian influence and the starch-plus-sauce meal pattern, and includes a Dec 2016 update after a reader (Elena) pointed out that palm oil/palm nut cream is the moambe and peanuts are less common than he assumed.
evidence.precision: Metric given for 6 of 11 ingredients (88 ml palm oil, 170 g paste, 411 g tomatoes, 237 ml water, 125 g peanut butter, 1.4-2 kg chicken). Onions sized only as '2 medium'. A cue or time on all 9 steps: oil 'shimmering, almost smoking', sear 4-5 min per side until golden, onions golden, garlic 30 sec until fragrant, paste 3 min until it darkens, 20 min covered, 10 min uncovered to 165F (74C). The only vessel named is a heavy Dutch oven, with no size. There is a typo ('2.5mm' ginger).
evidence.testing: A personal blog with no test kitchen. It does give reasons: very hot palm oil for colour, wiping the pot between batches so drippings don't burn, stirring the paste so the garlic doesn't scorch, mixing the peanut butter into a cup of hot sauce first so it blends, and an instant-read check at 165F. The author revised the post after reader feedback.
evidence.photos: Two images (a featured shot and one by the palm oil paragraph), no step photos. The author says he will add palm nut cream photos later, but none are there.
evidence.efficiency: States 15 min prep and 30 min cook (45 min total). Realistically about 55-60 min, since two batches of searing take roughly 20 min. No wasted steps; one pot.
evidence.access: Red palm oil is named with a US source (Nutiva Organic Red Palm Oil, Amazon or a co-op). Peanut oil is given as a substitute. The rest is ordinary US grocery stock.

winner.why: It has the most metric amounts, a cue on every step with a 165F finish, and a reason for each key move, though no candidate reached 60 because every English recipe swaps in peanut butter or gives few cues.

runnerUp.title: Congolese Chicken Moambe — Palm-Nut Chicken Stew

evidence.authenticity: Uses real palm-nut concentrate (500 g) as the sauce base, with no peanut butter, so the method is closer to traditional moambe. The author is a Filipino chef based in Singapore, with no Congolese background shown. The page gives no cultural context or dish history.
evidence.precision: Grams or ml for 9 of 10 ingredients (1,200 g chicken, 500 g concentrate, 250 g onion, 20 g garlic, 300 g tomato, 700 ml liquid, 10 g salt). Only 5 steps, with cues such as 'until pulpy', 'tender and fully cooked' and 'sauce coats the chicken'. No pan size, no temperatures, no heat levels.
evidence.testing: Labelled 'chef-tested', but the notes are thin: use concentrate not palm oil, stir so the thick sauce doesn't catch, reduce uncovered if loose. The reasoning is barely explained, and the authorship and provenance are not verifiable.
evidence.photos: One styled plated shot of chicken with rice and saka-saka, no process photos.
evidence.efficiency: 20 min prep and 60 min cook, with a simple one-pot method.
evidence.access: Palm-nut concentrate or palm butter is the key item. The page says it has no exact substitute and gives no US source.

runnerUp.why: It matches the traditional palm-nut sauce method with excellent amounts, but it loses to Explorers Kitchen on cues, reasoning, and access, and its provenance is thin.

notes: No recipe reaches 60. Serious Eats, NYT, ATK and BBC Good Food have no moambe recipe (BBC's palm nut chicken curry is Ghanaian). The English-language web is peanut-butter versions copied from one another (Margarita's -> Explorers Kitchen -> Travel Food Atlas, or food.com -> Denver Green Chili / Marty Made It), or palm-nut-concentrate recipes with thin precision (NKOSI, Sixto Carreon). Congolese cooks say the palm nut cream is the moambe; peanut butter makes the Mwambe Nsusu variant. None of the pages carries process photos, and none names a pan size. Pages that did not load, so they are unscored: internationalcuisine.com, afrik.com and 54flavours.com returned 403; congocookbook.com (the original that Recidemia and Alphabetical Recipes copy), bonvoyageurs.com and arousingappetites.com failed to fetch. The Congo Cookbook and 54 Flavours pages are worth checking by hand, since the palm-nut recipes there may score higher. NKOSI's read URL redirects to /congolese-moambe-recipe-chicken-in-palm-nut-sauce. It is a retailer page with one hero photo, a 400 g can of sauce graine, and a 'red oil rises to the surface' cue, but no US source or substitute. If the user will accept a palm-nut version and sources sauce graine from an African grocer, NKOSI's method pairs well with Explorers Kitchen's searing and tomato-paste steps. Winner score is 56, so status is none-found.
